chunks.briefTitle: Current route — Form 12 to the Pension Disbursing Authority
chunks.heading: Who this route is for
chunks.text: Form 12 is the application a spouse or co-authorised family member submits to the Pension Disbursing Authority to start family pension after a pensioner or family pensioner dies. The form's own header carries this description and cites the rule it is made under. The route applies when the claimant's name is already included in the Pension Payment Order. The rule directs the Pension Disbursing Authority to begin paying family pension, as authorised in the Pension Payment Order, to the widow or widower whose name has been included in that order.

chunks.briefTitle: Current route — Form 12 to the Pension Disbursing Authority
chunks.heading: What the claimant sends, and to whom
chunks.text: The claim goes to the Pension Disbursing Authority — in most cases the pension paying bank branch — not to the Head of Office. Rule 79(2)(a)(ii) names three things that accompany the claim: the claim in Form 12, a copy of the death certificate, and an undertaking to the bank in Format 9.

chunks.briefTitle: Current route — Form 12 to the Pension Disbursing Authority
chunks.heading: Timing stated in the rule
chunks.text: The Pension Disbursing Authority is directed to commence disbursement within one month of receiving the claim. Family pension becomes payable from the date following the date of death of the pensioner.

chunks.briefTitle: Current route — Form 12 to the Pension Disbursing Authority
chunks.heading: What Form 12 asks for
chunks.text: Form 12 asks for the name of the pensioner on whose death family pension is claimed, the date of death, the PPO number, the claimant's name, date of birth, relationship and postal address, and the bank account number, bank name and branch, and IFS code to which family pension is to be credited. Providing a PAN is requested on the form and providing an Aadhaar number is marked voluntary. SevaPath never collects either.

chunks.briefTitle: Alternative route — Form 10 to the Head of Office
chunks.heading: When the Head of Office route applies instead
chunks.text: Form 10 is the application made to the Head of Office for family pension. Its header cites several rules including rule 79. The rule sends the claim to the Head of Office in two situations: where the Pension Payment Order does not include the name of any member of the family for payment of family pension, and where the Head of Office is of the opinion that family pension has become payable to a member of the family other than the one named in the Pension Payment Order. This is why SevaPath treats Form 10 as the alternative route rather than the default. A spouse already named in the Pension Payment Order normally uses the Form 12 route to the Pension Disbursing Authority.

chunks.briefTitle: Alternative route — Form 10 to the Head of Office
chunks.heading: What the Head of Office does
chunks.text: On a claim in Form 10, the Head of Office is directed to sanction the family pension in Format 13, within one month of the date of receipt of the claim. Form 10 is also the route where a pensioner or family pensioner has gone missing, where a remarried widow or widower claims on behalf of minor children, where a guardian claims for a minor or a person with a mental disability, and where a Government servant died after retirement without the rule 57 or rule 58 forms having been submitted.

chunks.briefTitle: Alternative route — Form 10 to the Head of Office
chunks.heading: Documents listed on Form 10
chunks.text: Form 10 lists its own attachments, including proof of identity, proof of relationship with the deceased, details of family in Form 4, and an undertaking for refunding any excess payment made by the pension disbursing bank in Format 9. The list also requires a copy of the first page of the pass book showing name and account number, and states that the name of the claimant in the form and in the bank account should be the same.

chunks.briefTitle: Format 9 — undertaking to the bank about excess payment
chunks.heading: What Format 9 is
chunks.text: Format 9 is an undertaking addressed to the branch manager of the bank that will pay the pension. Its header cites the rules it is made under. In it, the signatory agrees to refund or make good any amount to which they are not entitled, or any amount credited to their account in excess of what they would be entitled to, and agrees to indemnify the bank against loss arising from crediting the pension to that account. Format 9 also has a line recording the date of birth of the spouse and a mark of identification.

chunks.briefTitle: Format 9 — undertaking to the bank about excess payment
chunks.heading: Why it is required
chunks.text: Rule 79(2)(a)(ii) names the undertaking to the bank in Format 9 as one of the three things that accompany a Form 12 claim, alongside the claim itself and a copy of the death certificate. Format 9 is required on the Form 10 route as well, so it is needed whichever route applies.

chunks.briefTitle: Format 9 — undertaking to the bank about excess payment
chunks.heading: What it does not do
chunks.text: Format 9 is an undertaking about repayment. Signing it does not establish eligibility for family pension and does not fix any amount. SevaPath does not compute or estimate any amount.

chunks.heading: Where Rule 79 sits
chunks.text: Rule 79 opens Chapter XII, headed "Sanction of family pension and residuary gratuity in respect of deceased or missing pensioners or family pensioner". The rule is titled "Sanction of family pension and residuary gratuity on the death or disappearance of a pensioner or family pensioner".

chunks.briefTitle: CCS (Pension) Rules, 2021 — Rule 79 flow after a pensioner's death
chunks.heading: The two branches of Rule 79(2)
chunks.text: Rule 79(2)(a) is the branch for a claimant whose name is already in the Pension Payment Order. The Pension Disbursing Authority commences disbursement, as authorised in the Pension Payment Order, on a claim in Form 12 with a copy of the death certificate and an undertaking in Format 9, within one month of receipt. Rule 79(2)(b) is the branch for a claimant whose name is not in the Pension Payment Order, or where the Head of Office considers family pension payable to someone other than the person named. The Head of Office sanctions family pension in Format 13 within one month of receiving a claim in Form 10. The same sub-rule covers the case where family pension was already being paid to a family pensioner who has since died or become ineligible, and a co-authorised disabled child, dependent parent or disabled sibling named in the Pension Payment Order then claims in Form 12.

chunks.briefTitle: CCS (Pension) Rules, 2021 — Rule 79 flow after a pensioner's death
chunks.heading: Adding names to the Pension Payment Order
chunks.text: Where the deceased pensioner is survived by a spouse together with permanently disabled children, dependent parents or disabled siblings whose names were not previously included in the Pension Payment Order, the Accounts Officer includes their names on a written communication from the Head of Office, made on a request from the spouse in Form 8.

chunks.briefTitle: CCS (Pension) Rules, 2021 — Rule 79 flow after a pensioner's death
chunks.heading: After sanction
chunks.text: On receiving a sanction under Rule 79, the Accounts Officer authorises payment within one month of receipt of the sanction. The Accounts Officer forwards a copy of the Pension Payment Order together with the Format 9 undertaking to the Central Pension Accounting Office within one month, that office issues a Special Seal of Authority within ten days, and the Pension Disbursing Authority acts to disburse within fifteen days of receiving it.

chunks.briefTitle: CCS (Pension) Rules, 2021 — Rule 79 flow after a pensioner's death
chunks.heading: A limit stated in the rule itself
chunks.text: A claim is not to be rejected on the ground that the family member's details are not available in Form 4 or in office records, if the Head of Office is otherwise satisfied about eligibility. A member of the family other than the widow or widower must submit the documents referred to in Rule 50(12)(b) along with the claim, in order to decide eligibility. Deciding eligibility is the department's function, not SevaPath's.

It is not in the current forms list. For a spouse named in the Pension Payment Order, the current route is a claim in Form 12 to the Pension Disbursing Authority under Rule 79(2)(a)(ii).

chunks.briefTitle: Form 14 is archived — do not use it as the current form
chunks.heading: Why people are still told to use Form 14
chunks.text: The Department's Frequently Asked Questions document, which predates the Central Civil Services (Pension) Rules, 2021, still answers the question "When does a family member become eligible for the grant of family pension?" by directing, in its own words, that "in case of death of a pensioner the wife/disabled child/ dependent parents/disabled siblings should apply in Form No. 14 to the pension disbursing authority". That FAQ answer is superseded by the 2021 Rules and by the current forms list. Where the FAQ and the 2021 Rules conflict, the 2021 Rules and the current forms list govern.

chunks.briefTitle: RBI Directions 2026 — how the bank should handle family pension
chunks.heading: Which document this is
chunks.text: These are the Reserve Bank of India directions to agency banks on disbursing Government pension, issued as RBI/DGBA/2026-27/399, reference CO.DGBA.GBD.No.S43/31.02.007/2026-27, dated 30 April 2026 and updated as on 24 June 2026. They apply to the banks authorised to disburse Central and State Government pension.

citations.issuer: Reserve Bank of India
citations.title: Reserve Bank of India [Disbursement of Government Pension by Agency Banks (ABs)] Directions, 2026 (Updated as on June 24, 2026)

chunks.briefTitle: RBI Directions 2026 — how the bank should handle family pension
chunks.heading: The bank must not insist on a new account
chunks.text: Agency banks shall not insist on opening a new account for credit of family pension after the death of the pensioner, if the spouse as family pensioner opts for an existing joint account for credit of family pension. This is useful to know before visiting the branch: if the pension was already being credited to a joint account, the surviving spouse can ask for family pension to be credited to that same account.

citations.issuer: Reserve Bank of India
citations.title: Reserve Bank of India [Disbursement of Government Pension by Agency Banks (ABs)] Directions, 2026 (Updated as on June 24, 2026)

chunks.briefTitle: RBI Directions 2026 — how the bank should handle family pension
chunks.heading: PPO number on the passbook
chunks.text: Agency banks shall record the PPO number in all pension passbooks of pensioners and family pensioners, and the direction names commencement of family pension to a spouse after the death of the pensioner as one of the situations this is meant to help with.

citations.issuer: Reserve Bank of India
citations.title: Reserve Bank of India [Disbursement of Government Pension by Agency Banks (ABs)] Directions, 2026 (Updated as on June 24, 2026)

chunks.briefTitle: RBI Directions 2026 — how the bank should handle family pension
chunks.heading: Recovery of excess payment
chunks.text: The Directions say banks may ensure that no recovery of an excess amount is effected without the pensioner's knowledge and consent, or without a prior notice, and any such recovery must conform to the applicable service rules. Where excess or wrongful payment arose from bank-attributed errors such as clerical errors, arithmetical miscalculations or incorrect application of instructions, the entire amount is to be credited to the Government account in lump sum immediately on detection. This is the backdrop to the Format 9 undertaking, which is the claimant's side of the same subject.

citations.issuer: Reserve Bank of India
citations.title: Reserve Bank of India [Disbursement of Government Pension by Agency Banks (ABs)] Directions, 2026 (Updated as on June 24, 2026)

citations.issuer: Reserve Bank of India

chunks.briefTitle: RBI Directions 2026 — how the bank should handle family pension
chunks.heading: Service expectations at the branch
chunks.text: Agency banks are directed to appoint nodal officers for pension grievances at each region or zone, and to have designated nodal officers for pension related complaints outside the Centralised Pension Processing Centres, together with a toll-free dedicated pension line.

chunks.heading: The three things the rule names
chunks.text: Rule 79(2)(a)(ii) names the claim in Form 12, a copy of the death certificate of the deceased pensioner, and an undertaking to the bank in Format 9.

chunks.briefTitle: What to gather for the Form 12 route
chunks.heading: The list printed on Form 12 itself
chunks.text: Form 12 carries its own list of documents to be submitted with it. The items that apply to a surviving spouse claiming in their own right are: - Two specimen signatures of the claimant, furnished on a separate sheet. A person who is not literate enough to sign may furnish two slips each bearing left hand thumb and finger impressions. - Two copies of passport size photographs of the claimant. - The undertaking for refunding any excess payment made by the pension disbursing bank. - A copy of the Pension Payment Order of the pensioner or previous family pensioner, to be provided if available. - A copy of the death certificate of the deceased pensioner or previous family pensioner.

chunks.briefTitle: What to gather for the Form 12 route
chunks.heading: Items that apply only when there is a guardian or nominee
chunks.text: Items 4, 5, 6 and 8 of the same list — specimen signature of the guardian, two self-attested photographs of the guardian or nominee, a descriptive roll of the guardian or nominee, and proof of permanent address of the guardian — apply where a guardian or nominee is involved, for example where the claimant is a minor or is suffering from a disorder or disability of mind. A surviving spouse claiming in their own right does not need the guardian items.

chunks.briefTitle: When the name on the record and the name on the bank account differ
chunks.heading: Why the names are expected to agree
chunks.text: The document list on Form 10 requires a copy of the first page of the pass book showing the name and account number to which family pension is to be credited, and states in the same item that the name of the claimant in the form and in the bank account should be the same. The Form 12 route rests on the claimant being the person whose name has been included in the Pension Payment Order, so the name on the Pension Payment Order matters too.

chunks.briefTitle: When the name on the record and the name on the bank account differ
chunks.heading: What a difference means, and what it does not
chunks.text: A difference in how a name is written across records — for example an extra middle initial on a bank record — is a discrepancy to be resolved with the office that issued the record. Nothing in the collected sources authorises a third party to decide that two differently written names are the same person. The Pensioners' Portal guidance on correcting a Pension Payment Order directs the pensioner to contact the Head of Office or the Pension Disbursing Agency for necessary action.

chunks.briefTitle: When the name on the record and the name on the bank account differ
chunks.heading: What SevaPath does
chunks.text: SevaPath shows both values exactly as they appear on the records, side by side, and marks the claim as needing human review. It does not choose between the values, does not merge them, does not normalise spelling, and does not decide whether the two names belong to one person. Resolving the difference is a task for the claimant with the Pension Disbursing Authority or the Head of Office.

chunks.briefTitle: What SevaPath will not answer
chunks.heading: Amounts
chunks.text: SevaPath does not calculate, estimate, or quote a family pension amount, a rate, a percentage, or arrears. The amount payable to a spouse named in the Pension Payment Order is the amount indicated in that Pension Payment Order, and the Pension Disbursing Authority disburses it as authorised there. Anyone asking what they will receive should read the Pension Payment Order and ask the Pension Disbursing Authority.

chunks.briefTitle: What SevaPath will not answer
chunks.heading: Eligibility
chunks.text: SevaPath does not decide whether anyone is eligible for family pension. Eligibility under the rules is determined by the department. The rules place that task with the Head of Office and set out what a claimant other than a widow or widower must submit in order for eligibility to be decided.

chunks.briefTitle: What SevaPath will not answer
chunks.heading: Identity
chunks.text: SevaPath does not certify identity, does not resolve a difference between two differently written names, and does not collect Aadhaar, PAN, account numbers, OTPs, passwords or payment details. The prototype uses synthetic records only.

chunks.briefTitle: What SevaPath will not answer
chunks.heading: Submission
chunks.text: SevaPath does not submit anything to any government system. Its output is a preparation summary the claimant carries to the Pension Disbursing Authority or the Head of Office. Any submission and receipt shown in the prototype is a demonstration.

chunks.briefTitle: What SevaPath will not answer
chunks.heading: Standing of this guidance
chunks.text: The Pensioners' Portal states that the information on it aims to give a general overview and is not a substitute for any rules, and advises consulting the original rules and orders for more specific information. SevaPath links to the originals for the same reason. The hackathon brief this prototype was built for requires the use of mock or synthetic data wherever personal information, payments, OTPs or government systems would normally be involved, and forbids presenting the prototype as an official government product.

chunks.briefTitle: What SevaPath will not answer
chunks.heading: The exact refusal wording
chunks.text: When the corpus does not support an answer, SevaPath replies exactly: `I could not verify this from the current official corpus.`

chunks.briefTitle: Which source wins when sources disagree
chunks.heading: The order SevaPath applies
chunks.text: 1. The Central Civil Services (Pension) Rules, 2021 as notified in the Gazette. This is the primary law for the journey SevaPath covers. 2. The current official form issued under those rules — Form 12, Form 10, Format 9 — for what a claimant actually fills in and attaches. 3. The Pensioners' Portal current forms list, for deciding which form is current and which is archived. 4. Reserve Bank of India directions, for what the bank must do on its side. 5. Departmental FAQs and general portal guidance, for background only.

chunks.briefTitle: Which source wins when sources disagree
chunks.heading: The known conflict in this corpus
chunks.text: The Department's FAQ document predates the 2021 Rules and still directs a claimant to Form 14. The 2021 Rules and the current forms list direct a spouse named in the Pension Payment Order to Form 12. By the order above, the 2021 Rules and the current forms list govern, and the FAQ answer is recorded only as superseded guidance so that SevaPath can warn about it.
